objectives.text: Read, write, order and compare common fractions and mixed numbers.
Find fractions of whole-number quantities and measurements.

lesson.title: Fractions and Mixed Numbers: Reading, Ordering, and Calculating
lesson.summary: This lesson covers reading, ordering, and comparing common fractions and mixed numbers. It also demonstrates how to find a fraction of a whole-number quantity or measurement using clear, step-by-step methods suitable for adult learners.

objectives.text: Read, write, order and compare common fractions and mixed numbers.
Find fractions of whole-number quantities and measurements.

sections.heading: Understanding Fractions and Mixed Numbers
sections.body: Fractions represent parts of a whole. The denominator shows how many equal parts exist, while the numerator shows how many parts you have. Mixed numbers combine a whole number with a fraction, such as 1 1/2. This format is common in cooking and measurements. Understanding these basics helps you read and write these numbers accurately in daily life and work settings.

sections.heading: Ordering and Comparing Values
sections.body: To compare fractions, look at the denominators first. If they are the same, the larger numerator is the bigger fraction. If denominators differ, convert them to a common denominator. For mixed numbers, compare the whole numbers first. If those are equal, compare the fractional parts. Ordering means arranging numbers from smallest to largest. This skill is useful when measuring ingredients or comparing distances.

sections.heading: Finding a Fraction of a Quantity
sections.body: To find a fraction of a whole number, divide the number by the denominator first. Then, multiply the result by the numerator. For example, to find one-third of twelve, divide twelve by three to get four. Then multiply four by one to get four. This method works for measurements too. If you need half of ten centimetres, divide ten by two to get five.

practice.prompt: A baker has 2 1/2 kg of flour and 3 1/4 kg of sugar. Which quantity is larger?
practice.explanation: Compare the whole numbers first: 3 is greater than 2, so 3 1/4 kg is larger than 2 1/2 kg.

practice.prompt: A carpenter needs to cut a 12-metre beam into equal sections. What is the length of one section if he takes one-third of the total length?
practice.explanation: Divide 12 by the denominator 3 to get 4, then multiply by the numerator 1 to get 4 metres.

practice.prompt: Order these fractions from smallest to largest: 1/4, 1/2, 3/4.
practice.explanation: Write one-half as 2/4, so the order is 1/4, 2/4, 3/4; therefore 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 is correct.
